question: Should `socket.drain` become a public Gateway event for both `sessions.subscribe` and `sessions.messages.subscribe`, and what slow-consumer behavior should it guarantee?
rationale: This adds an advertised Gateway event and changes teardown delivery/backpressure behavior for existing clients, which is a compatibility decision rather than a purely mechanical test fix.

options.title: Document and preserve compatibility
options.body: Keep the feature direction, but require one canonical helper, protocol docs, and tests proving existing slow session subscribers are not newly disconnected by default.

options.title: Accept stricter teardown delivery
options.body: Allow drain broadcasts to close slow clients during teardown, but document that as the explicit new contract before merge.

options.title: Pause this event surface
options.body: Close or defer the branch until maintainers decide whether session eviction telemetry belongs in this public Gateway event layer.

recommendation.title: Document and preserve compatibility
recommendation.body: Keep the feature direction, but require one canonical helper, protocol docs, and tests proving existing slow session subscribers are not newly disconnected by default.

likelyOwner.reason: The recent session event projection refactor makes this owner the best code-path decision point for where the public event and helper should live.
